title: 中国菜的绝活④完结·文思豆腐·切成几千根丝 | Signature Skill P4 · Tofu into 1,000 Threads 🔪
description:
你家乡有哪道「看着不可能」的绝活菜？评论区告诉我 / What's one seemingly-impossible craft dish from your hometown?

第④集·切（完结）—— 「中国菜的绝活」系列收官。一块嫩豆腐，切成几千根细如发丝的丝。
P4 · The Slice (finale) — the closing chapter of The Signature Skill. One block of soft tofu, cut into thousands of hair-thin threads.

嫩豆腐软到一碰就破，却要在刀下切成几千根发丝般的细丝，刀不停、豆腐不散——这功夫没有三五年练不成。它叫文思豆腐，是淮扬名菜，始于清代、已有三百多年；相传乾隆年间扬州天宁寺一位名叫文思的和尚善制豆腐（《扬州画舫录》有载），后来做进了满汉全席，成为宫廷与国宴名菜。细丝入清汤，入口即化。
捏（小笼包）、烫（过桥米线）、吹（北京烤鸭）、切（文思豆腐）——四道菜，四手绝活，这一季到此收官。
Soft tofu breaks at a touch, yet must be sliced into thousands of hair-thin threads with the knife never stopping and the block never falling apart — years to master. It's called Wensi tofu, a Huaiyang classic begun in the Qing dynasty, 300+ years old. Legend credits a monk named Wensi at Yangzhou's Tianning Temple in the Qianlong era, skilled at tofu dishes (recorded in the 《Yangzhou Huafang Lu》); it later entered the imperial Manchu-Han feast and state banquets. The threads drift into clear broth and melt in the mouth.
Pinch (dumplings), scald (crossing-bridge noodles), blow (Peking duck), slice (Wensi tofu) — four dishes, four hand-crafts. That closes this season.
